ai.purpose: RTT structural map of the paper 'We Can’t Agree to Disagree, Formally'.
ai.module.summary: This module exposes the regime structure behind the formalization of Aumann’s Agreement Theorem, connecting epistemic/Bayesian models, common-knowledge operators, and machine-checked proofs. It preserves the authors' results while adding RTT operators for agentic reasoning.

epistemic_model_regime.description: Agents are modeled via partitions, probability measures, and information sets.
epistemic_model_regime.evidence: Paper defines the standard Aumann framework of states, σ-algebras, and posteriors.

common_knowledge_regime.description: Common knowledge is captured via iterative knowledge operators and fixed points.
common_knowledge_regime.evidence: Formalization encodes common knowledge as a greatest fixed point of a knowledge operator.

agreement_theorem_regime.description: Aumann’s theorem: Bayesian agents with common priors and common knowledge of posteriors cannot agree to disagree.
agreement_theorem_regime.evidence: Main theorem is formalized and proved in the proof assistant.

formalization_regime.description: The entire argument is encoded in Lean (or similar), with kernel-verified proofs.
formalization_regime.evidence: Paper describes definitions, lemmas, and tactics used in the formal proof.

informal_vs_formal_reasoning.description: Classical textbook proofs vs fully formal, machine-checked proofs.
informal_vs_formal_reasoning.paper_alignment: Authors compare the informal Aumann proof with its formal counterpart.

intuitive_vs_symbolic_epistemics.description: Intuitive talk of “knowing” vs symbolic modal/measure-theoretic definitions.
intuitive_vs_symbolic_epistemics.paper_alignment: Formalization forces precise epistemic and probabilistic definitions.

local_beliefs_vs_global_structure.description: Individual posteriors vs global common-knowledge constraints.
local_beliefs_vs_global_structure.paper_alignment: Agreement theorem links local beliefs to global fixed-point structure.

informal_to_formal_transition.description: Translate the textbook Aumann proof into definitions and lemmas in the proof assistant.

epistemic_to_modal_transition.description: Recast knowledge and common knowledge in modal/fixed-point terms.
epistemic_to_modal_transition.paper_alignment: Common knowledge operator is defined and analyzed formally.

local_posterior_to_global_agreement_tran.description: Show that common knowledge of posteriors forces equality of beliefs.
local_posterior_to_global_agreement_tran.paper_alignment: Formal proof of the agreement theorem.

knowledge_operator.role: Maps events to what an agent knows at a given information partition.

common_knowledge_operator.role: Computes the greatest fixed point representing common knowledge of an event.

posterior_operator.role: Assigns Bayesian posteriors to agents given their information sets.

formal_proof_operator.role: Encodes the agreement theorem as a machine-checked proof object.

ai.audience: Researchers in epistemic logic, game theory, formal verification, and AI alignment.
